ENGINEERING NOTE · INFRASTRUCTURE SAFETY

Asking for force-destroy is not the same as receiving it.

A production safeguard should survive a mistaken input, not depend on everyone remembering the right value. This Terraform module makes destructive bucket removal impossible in production even when a caller explicitly requests it.

Platform
AWS data lake
Production rule
force_destroy is always false
Validation
Mocked Terraform plan

01 · THE HAZARD

A flexible variable can become a destructive escape hatch.

Terraform’s S3 force_destroy setting allows a non-empty bucket to be deleted. That convenience can be useful in a disposable development environment and dangerous in a production data lake.

Exposing the same Boolean everywhere leaves production safety dependent on a variable file, a command-line override or a rushed operator. The configuration accepts the request, even when the environment should never permit the outcome.

02 · THE GUARDRAIL

Derive the effective setting from environment policy.

The module distinguishes the requested value from the value resources actually receive. Development can honor the input, while production always resolves to false.

force_destroy_effective = (
  var.environment == "prod"
  ? false
  : var.force_destroy
)

The module also rejects unknown environments. That keeps a misspelled value from falling into a permissive default path.

03 · THE PROOF

Test the denied outcome, not only the happy path.

The strongest test deliberately supplies the dangerous combination: production plus force_destroy = true. A mocked provider allows Terraform to plan without AWS credentials, and the assertion verifies that the effective output is still false.

run "prod_refuses_force_destroy_even_when_asked" {
  command = plan

  variables {
    environment   = "prod"
    force_destroy = true
  }

  assert {
    condition = output.force_destroy_effective == false
  }
}

04 · THE LIMIT

A mocked plan proves configuration logic, not cloud behaviour.

The tests also cover least-privilege boundaries such as preventing the pipeline role from writing raw data and avoiding wildcard IAM actions. They are fast because the AWS provider is mocked.

That speed has a boundary: the suite proves the planned graph and policy logic, not a real AWS deployment. The next confidence layer would apply the stack in a sandbox account and run live permission checks before promotion.
